repairs.action: Added a net_cash rationale and rewrote the WACC rationale. Both now describe net cash as cash plus short- and long-term marketable investments less debt: $38.364B (F-455b2cbdf8) + $35.089B (S-0f9cbd5118 = F-e8f2f41b64 $5.070B + F-5368223b24 $30.019B) - $5.179B (S-0a86662e54) = $68.274B. Removed the round-1 caveat that long-term investments are excluded. Corrected the debt composition to current debt $0.491B + long-term debt including finance leases $4.688B. An in-memory dry run with the round-2 mapping (no files written, eu.py compute not run) confirmed short_term_investments 35,089M and net_cash 68,274M.

The net_cash rationale now states that the $12.895B noncurrent customer contract liabilities (F-3212bef088) are excluded from debt and treated as operating contract liabilities. Reasons given: the 10-K classifies them as contract liabilities with no significant financing component (quoted, periodic.txt ~line 2344), and they are conditional and can be retained if customers miss commitments (~line 1763). The rationale also states the counter-argument: the financing inflow of $12.747B (~line 2228) sits in cash, and the deposits are repayable 2029-2031 (~lines 1763, 2961), inside DCF years 3-5, so the exclusion favours the stock. It gives an analyst-arithmetic sensitivity of about -$11.3/share undiscounted (about -$8 discounted at WACC), roughly 1% of value. The WACC rationale no longer calls debt 'small' without qualification: it names the deposits and shows that net cash is still about $55.4B even if they are deducted.

Lowered the year-1 FCF margin from 55% to 50%; years 2-5 are unchanged. The fcf_margin rationale now quotes the 10-K capex guidance verbatim (periodic.txt line 1771, checked against the text: '...net of proceeds from government incentives, to be approximately $11.5 billion in the first quarter of 2027, approximately $25 billion in the first six months of 2027, and higher in the second half of 2027.'). It reconciles year 1 as labelled analyst arithmetic: NTM net income $188.7B (code) + D&A ~$12B + SBC ~$1.5B - net capex ~$55B - working capital ~$12B (receivables at 0.67x quarterly revenue) = ~$135B, about 50% of $269.5B, with a range of about 47-53.5%. The rationale states that 55% required floor capex and no working-capital build. It also notes that the Pillar Two tax payable flattered FY2026Q4 CFO and that customer deposits are financing flows, not CFO.

Checked citations against the round-2 narrative.json. Only Q-1 (revenue guidance) and Q-6 to Q-12 are cited, and their texts are unchanged. No GAAP or non-GAAP quotes (Q-2/3/4, Q-15/16/17) are cited, so no citation needed correcting.

notes: Inputs: peers INTC/AMAT/LRCX/KLAC; WACC 10.5%; terminal growth 3.0%; revenue growth for years 2-5 +5%/-10%/-15%/-5%; FCF margins 50/50/42/35/30% (year 1 was 55% in round 1); dcf_weight 0.75. Indicative in-memory dry run with the committed code and the round-2 mapping/assumptions (no files written; code is authoritative): net cash $68.274B; DCF EV $919.7B; terminal share of EV 55.9%; DCF value $862.8/share; peer median EV/Sales 15.1x; relative value $1,818.6/share; blended TP about $1,102 against the $1,035.84 close on 2026-10-08 (+6.4%, Neutral). The year-1 margin change lowers TP by about $8 against an asm-001-only recompute ($1,110); it is grounded in the capex reconciliation, not chosen for a target. FOR LEAD/WRITER: (1) The note should describe net cash as cash and short- and long-term marketable investments less debt, and drop the round-1 'rating would stay Neutral (not recomputed)' sentence; code now computes it. (2) The note should carry the customer-deposit exclusion as a valuation caveat (about $11/share if treated as debt-like, analyst arithmetic). (3) If the lead prefers debt-like treatment instead, gen-mapping would have to add ContractWithCustomerLiabilityNoncurrent (F-3212bef088, 12,895M) to total_debt. That would relabel 'debt' in the note as $18.1B, so I recommend keeping the exclusion plus the caveat. Unresolved: none in my scope.
